title: Decouple SealedSecret poller and add KMS envelope wrapping hook for DB credentials
author: Priya Patel
description: Motivation: On private deployments we observed long reconciliation loops and spiky Vault API traffic when the SealedSecret controller attempted to re-encrypt many DB credential secrets during rotation windows. This PR decouples the SealedSecret poller into a lightweight controller and introduces a KMS-envelope wrapping hook that uses the HSM-backed KMS plugin to wrap/unwrap database credentials during backup and rotation workflows. Goals: 1) reduce Vault/API thundering during cert/key rotations, 2) ensure DB credentials stored in SealedSecrets are additionally envelope-wrapped with the customer KMS key as an extra-at-rest protection, 3) provide a safe upgrade path with a reversible migration and automated rollback on failure. What changed: - Introduced sealedsecret-poller-shim controller (separate deployment) that watches only the SealedSecret status, performs low-cost diffs, and enqueues targeted re-encrypt tasks rather than full-list reconciliation. - Added kms-envelope-hook binary and Helm pre-upgrade/post-upgrade hook templates. The hook calls the HSM KMS plugin to create an envelope key, performs an extra layer of AES-GCM wrapping for secret.Value, and stores metadata in sealed-secret annotations (k8s.redwood.com/kms-envelope-v1). - Terraform: new module redwood_private_kms_hooks with IAM role and KMS policy templates for on-prem KMS proxies, plus outputs to inject into Helm values. - Helm chart: values options for enableSealedSecretShim, kmsEnvelope.enabled, hook concurrency and backoff controls. - Migration: a two-stage rollout. Stage A (dry-run): annotate existing SealedSecrets with kms-envelope=dry-run and run the hook in validation mode to verify unwrap via HSM without writing changes. Stage B (gradual apply): patch a percentage of namespaces via the rollout controller until success criteria met. Rollback: Helm hook supports safe revert by removing annotations and re-running original SealedSecret controller on failed migration nodes. Backwards compatibility: shim is opt-in and disabled by default; existing clusters are unaffected unless the operator toggles the values. Testing: integration test harness simulates 5k SealedSecrets and runs a rotation window; end-to-end used a local HSM emulator (SoftHSM v2) and a pre-prod HSM plugin binary. Performance: in our bench runs the average reconciliation loop CPU dropped by 62% and peak Vault API calls during rotation reduced by 88%. Security review: crypto review performed, envelope metadata includes keyID, nonce, and CSROVER (opaque mac). Docs: migration guide and troubleshooting section added to the installer docs under operations/secrets. Checklist: linear ENG-2041 tracks rollout, add e2e test to perf-canary, update runbook. References: Linear ENG-2041, Jira SUP-4729 for a customer incident that motivated this change.

release_notes: Introduce opt-in SealedSecret shim and KMS envelope wrapping hook to reduce reconciliation load during credential rotations; add Terraform module to configure KMS hook IAM bindings; Helm values to opt into migration; performance improvements and migration guide.
notes_for_ops: Enable enableSealedSecretShim=false by default. To opt-in: set kmsEnvelope.enabled=true and follow docs/operations/secrets/kms-envelope-migration.md. Monitor sealedsecret_shim_queue_length and kms_hook_failures. If HSM connectivity fails, hooks run in dry-run mode unless explicitly allowed.
rollback_instructions: Helm rollback will run the post-upgrade revert hook which removes kms-envelope annotations and re-enables original controller reconciliation for rolled-back namespaces; operator should monitor hook logs and manually trigger namespace-level revert if partial failures occur.
test_plan_summary: Unit tests for shim diffing logic and hook idempotency; integration runs with SoftHSM v2 across 5k SealedSecrets; terraform plan/validate; helm upgrade/dry-run scenarios; perf-canary job to validate Vault API call reduction.
